newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity down with natgas in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity down with natgas in thin trade.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading lower Monday in sympathy with weaker natural gas futures amid thin trade volume, industry sources said.
"The whole complex is fairly quiet right now, there's not a lot of news," said one New York based electricity futures trader.
As of 1200 EDT, June Palo Verde (PV) was trading down 26 cents at $18.10 per megawatt hour (MWh) after trade as low as $18.00, while July PV was down 25 cents at $22.55 per MWh.
September PV was down 28 cents at $22.75 per MWh.
June California Oregon Border (COB) was down 11 cents at $13.20 after reaching as low as $12.95, while July was steady at $15.70 per MWh.
Trade volume was not available from NYMEX as of midday Monday.

As of 1210, NYMEX June Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading down 3.6 cents at $2.09 per million British thermal units, giving some psychological weakness to electricity futures, the sources said.
Despite the Monday weakness in power futures, some traders continued to be bullish based on possible short-term power constraints in the U.S. West.
In California, Southern California Edison has said it could extend a refueling outage at its 1,080 megawatt San Onofre nuclear unit 3 for repairs to steam generators.

Also, near-term prospects for the Northwest power market was bolstered by talk that Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) would continue to limit its offers of daily surplus power well into May, market sources said.
In the Pacific Northwest, forecasters called for temperatures to average near or slightly below normal through the week with above normal precipitation.
In the Southwest, dry and very warm weather would settle over the southern part of the region with readings averaging six to 12 degrees Fahrenheit above normal.
Cloudy skies and seasonable temperatures were predicted for Utah, Colorado and northern California.
COB open interest for April 25 rose 152 to 4,654, while PV open interest fell 45 to 5,506, NYMEX said.
